request.system:
You are the extractor in Ledger, a system that documents legacy COBOL business rules so that a modern port can be written from the rules alone and checked against the running original.

Write business rules as Given/When/Then scenarios in plain English that a policy owner can read and approve. Hard requirements:

- Every clause cites the exact source lines it comes from (file plus [first, last] line numbers from the numbered listing; keep spans tight, normally 1-12 lines). If a statement cannot be sourced to specific lines, leave it out.
- Every clause lists the COBOL data names ("fields") and literal values ("literals": codes, messages, constants, without quotes) it relies on. Each listed field and literal must literally appear in the cited lines; a checker will reject the clause otherwise. Cite a declaration line (for example a PIC clause in WORKING-STORAGE) when the clause depends on a field's size or precision.
- Describe what the code actually does, not what it was probably meant to do. If the code has surprising behaviour (a later check overwriting an earlier result, a branch that can never run, arithmetic that truncates, a check that ignores something), state that behaviour precisely in the rule.
- Separate business logic from file plumbing. Opening/closing files, file-status checks, and abend handling are plumbing; leave them out unless they change a business outcome. Balance and record updates (for example 2700-*, 2800-*, 1050-* paragraphs) are business logic: a port that skips them would produce different output files.
- Be precise enough that a developer who never sees the COBOL could reproduce the outputs exactly: name the output fields set, the exact codes and message texts, the order of checks, signs and arithmetic (COBOL truncates toward zero unless ROUNDED is written), and which records are created versus updated.
- Keep each clause to one checkable fact. When a fact depends on a record layout, field size or precision, put it in its own clause that cites the declaration. Do not restate in one clause what another clause (or another part of the program) establishes.
- Use the field names exactly as declared. Use the tools to read any other paragraph or field layout you need; do not guess line numbers.

Return only rules for the unit you are given, at most the number requested, each one a distinct behaviour with an observable effect on the program's outputs.

Unit: CBTRN02C-main. Focus: The top-level flow: what happens to a transaction depending on the validation outcome, what a reject record contains, and the program's return code. Validation details and posting details are covered by other units.

content.text: {"rules":[{"title":"Route each daily transaction to posting or to the reject file, and set return code 4 when any are rejected","paragraph":"(main)","summary":"Each daily transaction record is counted and validated, starting with reason code 0 and a blank description. If the reason code is still 0 afterwards, the transaction is posted. Otherwise the reject count goes up and a 430-byte reject record is written: the original 350-byte input record followed by an 80-byte trailer holding the 4-digit reason code and its 76-character description. At the end of the run the program sets return code 4 if at least one transaction was rejected.","given":[{"text":"Records are read one at a time from the daily transaction file until end of file. Each record that is read adds 1 to the processed-transaction count.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[202,206],"fields":["END-OF-FILE","WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT"],"literals":["Y","N"]},{"text":"Before each transaction is validated, the failure reason code is set to 0 and the failure description is set to spaces, so nothing from the previous transaction carries over.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[208,210],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON","WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC"],"literals":["0"]},{"text":"The validation trailer is 80 bytes: a 4-digit unsigned numeric reason code followed by a 76-character description.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[180,182],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER","WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON","WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC"],"literals":[]},{"text":"A reject record is 430 bytes: 350 bytes of transaction data followed by an 80-byte validation trailer.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[176,178],"fields":["REJECT-RECORD","REJECT-TRAN-DATA","VALIDATION-TRAILER"],"literals":[]}],"when":[{"text":"After validation, the program checks whether the failure reason code is still 0.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[211,211],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON"],"literals":["0"]}],"then":[{"text":"If the reason code is 0, the transaction is posted.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[211,212],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON"],"literals":["0"]},{"text":"If the reason code is not 0, the reject count goes up by 1 and a reject record is written. The transaction is not posted.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[213,215],"fields":["WS-REJECT-COUNT"],"literals":["1"]},{"text":"The reject record's transaction data is the complete input daily transaction record, copied unchanged.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[447,447],"fields":["DALYTRAN-RECORD","REJECT-TRAN-DATA"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The reject record's trailer is the current reason code and description from validation.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[448,448],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER","VALIDATION-TRAILER"],"literals":[]},{"text":"The reject record is written as one record to the daily rejects file.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[451,451],"fields":["FD-REJS-RECORD","REJECT-RECORD"],"literals":[]},{"text":"Surprising behaviour: if the account rewrite fails during posting, reason code 109 and the description ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND are set. However, the main loop never checks the reason code after posting, so no reject record is written and the reject count does not increase. The code is cleared before the next transaction.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[554,559],"fields":["WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON","WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC"],"literals":["109","ACCOUNT RECORD NOT FOUND"]},{"text":"At the end of the run, the program displays the processed-transaction count and the reject count.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[227,228],"fields":["WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT","WS-REJECT-COUNT"],"literals":["TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :","TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :"]},{"text":"If at least one transaction was rejected, the return code is set to 4. Otherwise the program does not change the return code.","file":"CBTRN02C.cbl","lines":[229,231],"fields":["WS-REJECT-COUNT"],"literals":["4"]}]}]}
